title: Identifying Combinatorial Regulatory Genes for Cell Fate Decision via Reparameterizable Subset Explanations

problem.claim: Cell fate decisions are governed by complex interactions among numerous regulatory genes, and disruptions can cause developmental abnormalities and disease.

gap.claim: Traditional methods often fail to capture combinatorial regulatory-gene interactions and therefore cannot fully model cell fate dynamics.

contributions.claim: MetaVelo is a global feature explanation framework for identifying key regulatory gene sets influencing cell fate transitions.
MetaVelo uses a differentiable neural ODE surrogate and a controllable data-generation reparameterization to optimize explanations for black-box cell fate dynamics.
MetaVelo distinguishes independent from synergistic regulatory genes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe MetaVelo's distinction between independent and synergistic regulatory genes as offering novel insights into gene interactions governing cell fate.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across diverse stand-alone and longitudinal single-cell RNA-seq datasets and three black-box cell fate models, MetaVelo reportedly outperforms 12 baseline methods in predicting developmental trajectories and identifying combinatorial regulatory gene sets.
The authors report that MetaVelo provides a scalable and effective framework for developmental biology and therapeutic applications.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cell fate decisions involve coordinated interactions among many regulatory genes, with disruptions linked to disease and developmental abnormalities.
Existing methods inadequately capture combinatorial interactions in cell fate dynamics.
MetaVelo explains cell fate transitions using a black-box formulation, a differentiable neural ODE surrogate, and reparameterized controllable data generation.
Benchmarking on single-cell RNA-seq datasets and black-box models is reported to show superiority over 12 baselines.
The framework separates independent and synergistic genes and is presented as useful for developmental biology and therapeutic applications.

source_observation.claim: Reparameterizing a non-differentiable explanation problem as a controllable data-generation process enables optimization with a differentiable neural ODE surrogate.

interpretation.claim: A suitable differentiable surrogate and problem reparameterization can make black-box dynamical systems amenable to efficient feature-set explanation.

application.claim: This pattern may guide explanation methods for other black-box systems with temporal or dynamical behavior.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond the evaluated cell fate models and single-cell datasets.

source_observation.claim: The method reports distinguishing independent from synergistic regulatory genes.

interpretation.claim: Model explanations that represent interactions explicitly may reveal relationships missed by single-feature attribution.

application.claim: Interaction-aware explanations may support analysis of combinatorial mechanisms in other high-dimensional biological systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how independence and synergy are operationalized or validated.

unknowns: Exact benchmark metrics and numerical results are not provided.
The identities of the datasets, black-box models, regulatory genes, and baselines are not provided.
Details of the optimization procedure and validation of the reported gene interactions are not provided.
